findings.title: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing reuse
findings.body: The backup-code login path decrypts the whole `backupCodes` JSON array, sets the matching entry to `null`, and writes the entire re-encrypted array back with `prisma.user.update`. Because the read and write are not atomic (no transaction, no conditional update), two concurrent authorize() calls that both present the *same* code will both find it at a non-(-1) index and both succeed, defeating the single-use guarantee of a backup code. Two concurrent logins with *different* codes will also clobber each other, re-validating an already consumed code. Consider consuming the code inside a transaction or with an update guarded on the previous `backupCodes` value.

findings.title: Backup codes cannot be used by Google/SAML users with 2FA
findings.body: `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` (and the analogous check on the next line) only allows the second-factor flow to proceed when a TOTP code is present. Users who authenticate via Google/SAML and have 2FA enabled are redirected to `/auth/login?totp=<jwt>` with no password; if they submit a backup code (totpCode empty) they get `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` / `IncorrectEmailPassword` instead of being logged in. The login page also hides the "Lost access" button in that flow (`ExternalTotpFooter`), so for these accounts backup codes are generated and stored but can never be redeemed — exactly the lock-out case the feature is meant to solve. The condition should also accept `credentials.backupCode`.

findings.title: onEnable() is only called from the Close button, so dismissing the dialog leaves stale UI and loses codes
findings.body: Previously `onEnable()` fired as soon as the enable API returned 200. Now the success path only calls `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and `onEnable()` is invoked exclusively by the "Close" button handler. If the user dismisses the dialog with ESC, the X, or an overlay click (which triggers `onOpenChange`), 2FA is already enabled server-side but the parent settings view is never notified, so the two-factor switch stays in the "off" state until a manual reload. The user also loses the only display of their backup codes, with no way to regenerate them. `onEnable()` should be called when the code is accepted (or on `onOpenChange` while on the backup-codes step).

findings.title: "missing_backup_codes" tells users to generate codes in settings, but no such feature exists
findings.body: `"missing_backup_codes": "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings."` is shown when `user.backupCodes` is null — which is the case for every account that enabled 2FA before this change, and for anyone who already spent all ten codes. There is no regenerate/backup-codes screen in settings: codes are only created by `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup`, which rejects accounts that already have 2FA enabled (`TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`). The only actual remedy is to disable and re-enable 2FA, so the message sends users on an impossible errand. Either add a regeneration path or change the text to describe the real recovery procedure.

findings.title: Backup codes stored with reversible encryption instead of hashed
findings.body: `backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` persists the plaintext codes under a single application-wide key, and both the login and disable paths decrypt them to compare. Unlike `twoFactorSecret`, backup codes never need to be recovered in cleartext — verification only requires an equality check — so they should be stored as hashes (e.g. bcrypt/sha-256 per code). As written, anyone who obtains the database plus `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (one secret shared by every other encrypted field) gets a usable 2FA bypass for every user.

findings.title: Submitting an empty/short backup code silently does nothing
findings.body: The login form is rendered with `noValidate`, so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the backup-code input (apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx) are never enforced, and the zod schema `passthrough()`es `backupCode` without validation. Submitting the backup-code step with an empty field sends `backupCode: ""`, the server falls through to the TOTP branch and throws `SecondFactorRequired`, which this handler maps to `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` — a no-op since it is already true — leaving no error message and no visible feedback. Add client-side validation for `backupCode` (or surface `SecondFactorRequired` as an error while in the lost-access state).

findings.title: Unvalidated request body can crash the disable endpoint with a 500
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes the field is a string. A client that posts `{"backupCode": 123}` or `{"backupCode": {}}` passes the truthiness check and then throws `TypeError: replaceAll is not a function`, producing an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. Likewise `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` on line 58 throws if the stored value cannot be decrypted/parsed (e.g. after an encryption-key rotation). Validate/coerce the body (zod or `typeof === "string"`) and wrap the decrypt/parse in a try/catch returning a defined ErrorCode.

findings.title: Passing type="password" to PasswordField disables the show/hide toggle
findings.body: `PasswordField` computes `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` and then spreads `{...props}` *after* it (packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx), so the explicit `type="password"` kept from the old `TextField` usage overrides the computed value. Clicking the eye icon toggles `isPasswordVisible` but the input stays `type="password"`, i.e. the reveal button does nothing. Drop the `type` prop here.

findings.title: tabIndex={-1} makes the password reveal button keyboard-inaccessible
findings.body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide-password button removes it from the tab order for all `PasswordField` consumers across the app (login, signup, 2FA modals). Keyboard-only and screen-reader users can no longer reach this control even though it has an `sr-only` label, which is an accessibility regression affecting every password input, not just the 2FA dialogs. If the goal was to stop the button from stealing focus during the 2FA flow, make it opt-in via a prop instead of changing global behaviour.

findings.title: resetState leaves stale form/backup-code state and leaks the blob URL
findings.body: `resetState()` clears only `password`, `errorMessage` and `step`. The component is not unmounted when the dialog closes (state lives above the Radix `Dialog`), so `form`'s `totpCode`, `backupCodes`, `secret`, `dataUri` and `backupCodesUrl` persist. Consequences: (1) the previously entered 6-digit `totpCode` is still in the form on a subsequent setup, so pressing "Enable" immediately submits the stale code; (2) the object URL created with `URL.createObjectURL` is only revoked on the next successful setup, so it (and the plaintext backup codes it contains) is retained for the lifetime of the document. Reset the form (`form.reset()`) and clear/revoke the backup-code state too.

findings.title: No test covers the core new behaviour: authenticating with a backup code
findings.body: The added test steps only exercise the download/copy/close buttons on the new backup-codes screen; the primary feature paths — logging in through "Lost access" with a backup code (including that a code is consumed and cannot be reused) and disabling 2FA with a backup code — are left as a TODO comment. Given the security sensitivity (single-use enforcement, re-encryption of the remaining codes, dash stripping), at least one end-to-end or unit test for a successful and a repeated backup-code redemption should be part of this PR.

findings.title: Assertion on the 2FA switch is a no-op and was documented rather than fixed
findings.body: `expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on the Promise returned by `isChecked()`, which is always truthy, so this step can never fail — as the newly added FIXME admits. Since the enable flow now ends on the backup-codes dialog (the switch is not updated until `onEnable` runs), this test would not catch a regression where 2FA is never actually enabled. Replace it with `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch][data-state="checked"]')).toBeVisible()` as the second test already does.

findings.title: Backup-code component is exported under the name TwoFactor
findings.body: The new component in `BackupCode.tsx` is declared as `export default function TwoFactor({ center = true })`. The copy-pasted name makes React DevTools, error stacks and future greps report this backup-code input as "TwoFactor", which is confusing next to the real `TwoFactor` component it is rendered alongside in login.tsx and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx. Rename it to `BackupCode`.
